title: Orvell Travel: Smart UI catalog
description: Components an assistant may answer with, built only from this system's tokens. Generated by OpenDesigner smartui.py catalog; do not edit.
instructions: Answer in plain text first. Show a component only when it does a job text cannot: a list to pick from, numbers to compare, a form to fill, a step to approve. When the person asks to see several records (which invoices, my orders), show them in a list or table, not bullets, even two. A question about one thing (when is the next invoice due?) is a short factual answer and stays text (R1). One component per answer unless the person asked for more (R2). Actions that change data (book, pay, send, delete) are buttons the person presses; never claim they happened (R3). Use only the components and properties in this catalog; there are no colour, size, style, class or URL-of-your-choice properties (R4). Every number must come from the data you were given; leave a value out when you do not have it (R6). Text is plain: no HTML or markdown.

AnswerSources.description: A written answer in a few short paragraphs, each with small numbered chips that point to the sources listed under it.

opendesigner.name: Answer with sources
opendesigner.use: for an assistant's answer that has to show where each statement comes from
use_when: an answer drawn from documents, policies or pages, where the person may want to check each statement
avoid_when: a short factual answer that fits in one sentence: answer in plain text
only the list of sources, with no answer: use citation-list
one term or idea explained in a few lines: use summary-card

KeyFacts.description: The facts about one thing as label and value rows, with a short note where it helps and a status colour on values that are a status.

opendesigner.name: Key facts
opendesigner.use: to give the details of one booking, order, place or product at a glance
use_when: the person asks for the details of one thing: a flight, a parcel, an apartment, a plan
avoid_when: several things side by side: use comparison
two to four headline numbers for a period: use kpi-strip
a step-by-step status over time: use progress-status

SummaryCard.description: One term, plan or policy explained: what kind of thing it is, a short summary, up to four key points and other names it goes by.

opendesigner.name: Summary card
opendesigner.use: to define a term or sum up one policy, plan or document in a few lines
use_when: the person asks what something means, or wants one plan, policy or document summed up
avoid_when: an answer that has to cite where each statement comes from: use answer-sources
the details of a booking or product as label and value: use key-facts
two or more things compared: use comparison

CitationList.description: Numbered sources on their own: title, publisher and date, a short excerpt where it helps, and a button to open each one.

opendesigner.name: Citation list
opendesigner.use: to list the sources behind an answer, or reading to follow up on
use_when: the person asks where an answer came from, or for sources or further reading on a topic
avoid_when: an answer with its sources: use answer-sources
files the person can download: use file-card
search results to choose from: use result-list

DataTable.description: A plain table of up to 50 rows with a title and a summary line, sortable by any column and shown ten rows to a page.

opendesigner.name: Data table
opendesigner.use: for a list of records an assistant or a report fills in, such as invoices, orders or transactions
use_when: an answer that lists records with the same few fields, where the person may want to sort or page through them
avoid_when: two to four headline totals: use kpi-strip
numbers over time: use line-chart or bar-chart
a handful of options to pick from: use result-list or comparison
rows the person must select and act on in bulk: use receipts-table

BarChart.description: Six months of spend as bars, with the current month's forecast hatched on top, a dashed budget line and a tooltip on the bar you point at.

opendesigner.name: Monthly spend chart
opendesigner.use: for monthly spend or usage against a budget, with a forecast
use_when: a billing or usage page that must warn early when the month is heading over budget
avoid_when: a share of a whole, such as spend by team: use donut-breakdown
a few headline numbers with no monthly history: use kpi-strip or budget-meters
more or fewer than six periods: the columns are fixed at six

LineChart.description: One or two values over time as lines on a light grid, with the highest and lowest marked and a button that shows the same numbers as a table.

opendesigner.name: Line chart
opendesigner.use: for a trend over time, such as a price, a usage figure or a measurement week by week
use_when: an answer about how one or two numbers changed over 2 to 24 periods
avoid_when: amounts per period to compare side by side, or against a budget: use bar-chart
a share of a whole: use donut-breakdown
one current number with no history: use kpi-strip

DonutBreakdown.description: Spend split into four categories as a donut with the total in the middle, and a legend that lists each amount and share.

opendesigner.name: Spend breakdown donut
opendesigner.use: for showing how a total splits into a few categories
use_when: a billing or usage page that needs the total and each category's amount and share side by side
avoid_when: more than four categories, or values to compare over time: use bar-chart
a few headline numbers with no part-of-a-whole split: use kpi-strip
spending against limits per category: use budget-meters

KpiStrip.description: Four headline numbers in one band, each with a plain note under it, and a small bar where a share matters.

opendesigner.name: Stat strip
opendesigner.use: at the top of a dashboard, for its headline numbers
use_when: a report or account page that opens with two to four totals before the detail
avoid_when: one number tracked against a limit or goal: use budget-meters or savings-goal
numbers over time: use bar-chart
a share of a whole split into parts: use donut-breakdown

ProgressStatus.description: Where something stands: a status line coloured by its tone, an optional progress bar, the steps done and still to come, and when it was last updated.

opendesigner.name: Progress status
opendesigner.use: to answer where an order, refund, request or job is right now
use_when: an answer to 'where is my order', 'is it done yet' or 'what happens next', with one status and a few steps
avoid_when: a list of tasks the person still has to do: use setup-steps
a finished action with its reference number: use receipt
something that failed and can be retried: use error-retry
a live delivery on a map: use delivery-tracker

Comparison.description: Two to four options side by side: each with its name, price and a Choose button, then one row per attribute so the differences line up.

opendesigner.name: Comparison
opendesigner.use: when someone is choosing between a few fares, plans or memberships and wants the differences in one view
use_when: two to four options of the same kind that differ on a few named attributes, such as fare types or plan tiers
avoid_when: more than four options or a long list to browse: use result-list
one item and its details: use product-card
options that only need a name to pick from: use quick-replies

ResultList.description: Up to eight results as cards: a photo, the name, one meta line, an optional detail and badge, a price and one button each.

opendesigner.name: Result list
opendesigner.use: when someone asks to find or be shown a few places, stays, products or services and will open one
use_when: a short list of results to scan and open one: stays, restaurants, products, classes or venues
avoid_when: two to four options compared on the same attributes: use comparison
one item in detail: use product-card
rows of records with many columns: use data-table

ProductCard.description: A card for one product: a photo, category, name, one-line description, rating, price with the old price struck out, an Add to bag button and a save toggle.

opendesigner.name: Product card
opendesigner.use: in a store or marketplace grid
use_when: a featured product or add-on shown on its own, with a quick add and save
avoid_when: several saved items in a grid: use wishlist-grid
the full product page with several photos: use product-gallery
a dish on a menu: use menu-item

QuickReplies.description: An optional question and two to six short answers as chips, so the person can reply with one tap instead of typing.

opendesigner.name: Quick replies
opendesigner.use: under an assistant's message, when the next reply is one of a few known answers
use_when: the assistant asks a question whose answer is one of two to six short options, such as a day, a size or a next step
avoid_when: options that need prices or details to choose between: use comparison or result-list
a free answer is likely: ask in text and let the person type
more than six answers: use a list or a select field in form-fields

FormFields.description: A short form of one to eight fields (text, number, choice, date or switch) with hints, checks as you leave a field, and Continue and Cancel buttons.

opendesigner.name: Form fields
opendesigner.use: when the assistant needs a few details it cannot guess, such as a delivery change, a request or a problem report
use_when: two to eight details the person must give before the assistant can act, each a short text, a number, a choice from a list, a date or a yes or no
avoid_when: one choice from a few answers: use quick-replies
picking an appointment time: use time-slots
signing in or anything with a password: use sign-in-form, and never ask for a password in a generated form
confirming an action that pays, sends or deletes: use approval-prompt after the form

SetupSteps.description: A short list of first steps with progress: what is done, the one step to do now with its time and a way to skip, and what comes next.

opendesigner.name: Setup checklist
opendesigner.use: for a new account's first steps
use_when: a home-screen card that brings people back to an unfinished setup, one step at a time
avoid_when: steps an AI agent is running on its own: use agent-steps
a long form split into pages with back and next: build it from the form's own sections
a daily habit or goal: use daily-goals or habit-tracker

TimeSlots.description: Free times grouped by day, one button per time, with the time zone stated and a plain line for a day with nothing free.

opendesigner.name: Time slots
opendesigner.use: when someone wants to book or move an appointment and needs to pick one of the free times
use_when: picking one free time for an appointment, a call or a delivery window, over one to seven days
avoid_when: picking a date range or dates months ahead: use date-range-picker
a day's existing plan to read: use calendar-agenda
only two or three times: quick-replies may be enough

ApprovalPrompt.description: Asks the person before something that changes data happens: what will happen, the details that matter, a warning when it cannot be undone, and Cancel or the action itself.

opendesigner.name: Approval prompt
opendesigner.use: just before an action that sends, pays, books or deletes, so the person confirms it first
use_when: an assistant is about to do something that changes data (send, pay, book, delete) and the person must say yes first
avoid_when: the action already happened: use receipt
the person still has to fill in values: use form-fields
a bill or request that goes through several approvers: use approval-panel

Receipt.description: What just happened: a status line in its tone, what was done, a reference number, the lines that matter, a total, a note and up to two next steps.

opendesigner.name: Receipt
opendesigner.use: right after a booking, payment, order or change went through (or did not), to say what happened
use_when: an action finished and the person needs the outcome, its reference number and what to do next
avoid_when: the action has not happened yet and needs a yes: use approval-prompt
the action failed and can be tried again: use error-retry
a long history of payments or orders: use data-table

ErrorRetry.description: Says in plain words what failed and that nothing else broke, with an optional error code, a Try again button and one other way forward.

opendesigner.name: Error with retry
opendesigner.use: when a load, search or action failed and trying again may work
use_when: something the person asked for failed (a load, a search, a payment that did not start) and trying again may work
avoid_when: the action went through, or was refused for a known reason: use receipt with the danger tone
a list loaded and is simply empty: use empty-state
a warning about something that has not failed yet: use approval-prompt

EmptyState.description: What a list shows when there is nothing in it: a small drawing in the system's own colours, what it means, when that changes, and one thing to do.

opendesigner.name: Empty state
opendesigner.use: when a list or page has nothing in it yet
use_when: a list someone has cleared, where the message should say all is done and when new items will arrive
avoid_when: something went wrong loading the list: use alert-banners with a retry action
a first-run checklist of several steps to get going: use setup-steps
a short notice above a list that still has items: use alert-banners

ImageCard.description: One photo with a caption, an optional credit line and an optional button, for when the answer is a picture of something.

opendesigner.name: Image card
opendesigner.use: when an answer is best shown as one photo of a place, dish, product or room, with a line about it
use_when: the person asked to see something, and one photo with a line of context answers it
avoid_when: several photos or options to choose between: use result-list
a product with a price to buy: use product-card
a place to find: use location-card

LocationCard.description: A place without a third-party map: its name and address over a drawn street pattern with a pin, how far it is, its opening hours and an Open in maps button.

opendesigner.name: Location card
opendesigner.use: when an answer is one place to go: a shop, a clinic, a restaurant or a pick-up point
use_when: the person asked where something is, and one place with its address and hours answers it
avoid_when: several places to compare or choose from: use result-list
a photo of the place is the point: use image-card
a route with steps or a live map is needed: hand off to a maps app with the Open in maps event

FileCard.description: One file to download: an icon for its kind, the file name, its type and size, an optional date, Download and an optional Preview.

opendesigner.name: File card
opendesigner.use: when an answer hands over a file: a statement, an export, a signed contract or an image
use_when: the assistant made or found one file the person can download, such as an export or a statement
avoid_when: several files to pick from: use data-table
the person must upload a file: use file-dropzone
the content itself should be read here: use summary-card or code-block

CodeBlock.description: A piece of code with its file name and language, a Copy button, and long lines that scroll sideways inside the box.

opendesigner.name: Code block
opendesigner.use: to show a command, a snippet or an example request the person can copy
use_when: the answer includes a command, a config file, a snippet or an example request the person will run or paste
avoid_when: a short command name inside a sentence: keep it in the text
a file the person downloads: use file-card
a form the person fills in: use a form part

FlightResults.description: A list of flight options: departure and arrival times and airports, the duration over a stops line, the airline as a drawn mark, the price, Best and Cheapest tags, and sort chips.

opendesigner.name: Flight results
opendesigner.use: on a flight search results page, for comparing and choosing a flight
use_when: a short list of journeys of any kind where time, stops and price decide the pick
avoid_when: the pass for a flight already booked: use boarding-pass
the search form before results: use trip-search
hotel or home results: use stay-card

Column.description: Two to four parts one under the other, only when the person asked for more than one.
